item: BDD TDD for LLM Agent Testing
best_architecture: Three-layer testing pyramid. (1) UNIT LAYER (mocked, deterministic): inject fake LLM at boundary, mock at HTTP seam via respx for OpenAI-compatible endpoint, use vcrpy/pytest-recording cassettes for replay. Assert on structure/tool-routing, NOT free text. (2) INTEGRATION LAYER (real model, semantic assertions): assert on invariants and properties (schema validity, tool-call presence, FAIL_TO_PASS transitions) rather than literal equality; gate fuzzy claims through LLM-as-judge (DeepEval G-Eval). (3) EVAL/BENCHMARK LAYER: SWE-bench-style execution oracle - did the patch make failing tests pass without breaking passing tests? pytest-bdd preferred over behave/Robot (full pytest ecosystem: fixtures, xdist, markers for mocked vs live separation). For Local-Claw's polyglot setup, the TypeScript MCP server is tested with vitest + @langwatch/scenario, the Python orchestrator with pytest-bdd, and Rust/TS/Python skills are validated at the eval layer via their own native test runners invoked through the execution oracle, so each language keeps its idiomatic toolchain while the BDD scenarios live in the orchestrator as the single source of behavioral truth.
reference_papers: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code / HumanEval (Chen et al. 2021) - arxiv:2107.03374 - defines the unbiased pass@k estimator and execution-based functional-correctness evaluation
SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues? (Jimenez et al. 2023) - arxiv:2310.06770 - FAIL_TO_PASS / PASS_TO_PASS execution oracle for agentic code patches
AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents (Liu et al. 2023) - arxiv:2308.03688 - multi-environment agent evaluation, execution-trace-style scoring
SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering (Yang et al. 2024) - arxiv:2405.15793 - agent harness design and tool-use evaluation
G-Eval: NLG Evaluation using GPT-4 with Better Human Alignment (Liu et al. 2023) - arxiv:2303.16634 - LLM-as-judge scoring used by DeepEval's GEval metric
RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation (Es et al. 2023) - arxiv:2309.15217 - reference-free metric battery for RAG/agent retrieval steps
Self-Preference Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge (Wataoka, Takahashi & Ri 2024) - arxiv:2410.21819 - quantifies self-grading bias (rooted in low-perplexity familiarity); motivates cross-family judge selection
LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations (Panickssery et al. 2024) - arxiv:2404.13076 - shows judges self-recognize and overrate own outputs, reinforcing the no-self-judge rule

key_libraries: pytest (Python, >=8.x) - base test runner and fixture/marker engine
pytest-bdd (Python, >=7.x) - Gherkin feature files + step definitions inside pytest; preferred over behave for fixture/xdist/marker reuse
pytest-asyncio (Python, >=0.24, asyncio_mode=auto) - drives async agent/orchestrator coroutines; pin event-loop scope to match fixture scope to avoid 'Event loop is closed' teardown races
pytest-mock (Python, latest) - mocker fixture for injecting the fake LLM at the boundary
respx (Python, >=0.21) - mocks the httpx-based OpenAI-compatible endpoint at the HTTP seam
vcrpy + pytest-recording (Python) - record/replay real model HTTP exchanges as cassettes (@pytest.mark.vcr)
deepeval (Python, latest) - GEval LLM-as-judge metric and assert_test; configure a separate judge model to avoid self-grading
hypothesis (Python, >=6.x) - property-based generation of adversarial prompt/tool inputs
pytest-xdist (Python, latest) - parallelize the mocked unit suite; keep live suite serial to control GPU contention
langwatch-scenario / @langwatch/scenario (Python + TypeScript) - scripted agent scenario simulation across the polyglot boundary
vitest (TypeScript, >=2.x) - test runner for the MCP server, paired with @langwatch/scenario
pitfalls: Asserting on literal output text. Any exact-string assertion on model prose breaks on every model version, temperature, fine-tune, or batch-size change. Assert on structure (parsed JSON schema, tool name + argument shape, FAIL_TO_PASS transitions) and route fuzzy prose claims through an LLM-judge with a numeric threshold instead.

VCR cassette staleness. A recorded cassette replays a frozen response that no longer matches real model behavior after the model is fine-tuned or upgraded, so the unit test stays green while production has silently drifted. Tag cassettes with the model id/version, periodically re-record under a 'record-once' mode in CI, and pair every cassette-backed unit test with a (gated) live test that re-validates the same invariant.

temperature=0 false determinism. Greedy decoding only removes sampler randomness; outputs still vary because dynamic batching changes the reduction order of non-associative float ops (batch size > 1, tensor parallelism, different GPU/dtype/engine version all shift results). Do NOT assume bit-identical output at temp=0. For deterministic unit tests, mock the model entirely. For self-hosted determinism, pin vLLM version + dtype + hardware and set VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 (CC>=8.0) and VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0; for hosted APIs pin the seed and verify the returned system_fingerprint. Expect ~95-99%, not 100%, reproducibility - prefer tolerance/property assertions over equality.

Test-oracle gap. FAIL_TO_PASS alone does not catch semantic regressions that still keep the test green (e.g., the agent hardcodes the expected value, deletes the assertion, or weakens the test). Always pair FAIL_TO_PASS with PASS_TO_PASS (previously-passing tests must stay green), guard against test-file tampering, and add a held-out hidden test set the agent never sees.

LLM-judge circularity / self-preference bias. Using the same model (or same family) as both agent-under-test and judge causes systematic over-rating - judges self-recognize and favor their own low-perplexity generations (arxiv:2410.21819, arxiv:2404.13076). For Local-Claw, never let Gemma judge Gemma or Qwen judge Qwen; use a cross-family judge model and periodically calibrate judge scores against human-labeled samples.

Scenario scope too large. One Gherkin scenario that spans ten agent steps is impossible to diagnose when it fails - you cannot tell which step regressed. Keep scenarios to a single behavioral assertion (one tool-routing decision, one summarization quality check); use Scenario Outlines for variations and Background for shared setup rather than chaining steps.

Marker leakage. Live/eval tests requiring a GPU or real model accidentally run in CI (no GPU) and hang until timeout, blowing up the pipeline. Register explicit markers (live, gpu, eval), default-deselect them ('-m "not live"'), gate them behind an env flag (LIVE_TESTS=1), and add a hard per-test timeout (pytest-timeout) so a hung live test fails fast instead of stalling the run.

Non-idempotent fixtures / shared agent state. The agent writes to shared MongoDB (or filesystem) state and the next test observes the previous test's residue, producing order-dependent flakiness. Use per-test database/namespace isolation, transactional rollback or a fresh ephemeral container per test, and assert a clean baseline in fixture setup - never rely on test execution order.

Async fixture teardown race. With pytest-asyncio the event loop can be torn down before cleanup coroutines (closing httpx clients, killing the agent subprocess, draining the MCP connection) finish, raising 'RuntimeError: Event loop is closed' or leaking processes. Use the built-in event_loop fixture (do not define a competing custom loop), set event-loop scope to match the fixture scope, and await all cleanup before yielding control back; verify subprocess/clients are actually closed in teardown.

(Polyglot-specific) Mixing test runners across the boundary. Driving the TypeScript MCP server from pytest via brittle subprocess shells loses structured failures and stack traces. Keep each language in its idiomatic runner (vitest for TS, pytest-bdd for Python, cargo test for Rust) and let the orchestrator's BDD scenarios assert only on the cross-process contract (MCP tool schema, JSON-RPC responses), not on internal language details.
bdd_gherkin_scenarios:
Feature: Mocked LLM tool routing (unit layer, deterministic)
  As the orchestrator I must route a task to the correct MCP tool with a valid argument schema, independent of model prose.

  @mocked
  Scenario: Agent routes a file-edit task to the correct MCP tool
    Given a fake LLM that returns a tool call "edit_file" with arguments {"path": "src/app.py", "content": "..."}
    And the OpenAI-compatible endpoint is mocked with respx
    When the agent receives the task "add a docstring to app.py"
    Then exactly one MCP tool call is emitted
    And the tool name is "edit_file"
    And the tool arguments validate against the edit_file JSON schema
    And no assertion is made on the model's natural-language explanation

Feature: LLM-judge semantic quality (integration layer, real model, gated)
  Summaries produced by the real local model must meet a coherence bar without literal-string comparison.

  @live @gpu
  Scenario: Real Gemma produces a coherent code summary
    Given the real Gemma model is loaded and LIVE_TESTS=1
    And a DeepEval GEval coherence metric using a cross-family judge model (not Gemma)
    When the agent summarizes the module src/orchestrator.py
    Then the GEval coherence score is greater than or equal to 0.8
    And the summary mentions at least one public function name from the module

Feature: Execution-based coding oracle (eval/benchmark layer)
  A code patch is correct only if it turns the failing test green without breaking passing tests.

  @eval @live
  Scenario Outline: Agent patch satisfies the FAIL_TO_PASS / PASS_TO_PASS oracle
    Given a repository with a known failing test "<fail_test>"
    And a set of currently-passing tests "<pass_tests>"
    When the agent applies a patch to fix "<fail_test>"
    Then running pytest shows "<fail_test>" transitions from fail to pass (FAIL_TO_PASS)
    And all of "<pass_tests>" remain passing (PASS_TO_PASS)
    And the patch does not modify the test files

    Examples:
      | fail_test                     | pass_tests                          |
      | tests/test_parser.py::test_a  | tests/test_parser.py::test_b        |
      | tests/test_api.py::test_route | tests/test_api.py::test_health      |

Feature: Marker-based live/mocked separation (CI hygiene)
  The mocked suite must be fast and GPU-free; live evals must be opt-in.

  @mocked
  Scenario: Default CI run executes only the fast mocked suite
    Given the test command "pytest -m 'not live and not eval'"
    When the suite runs on a CI runner with no GPU
    Then no real model is loaded
    And the mocked suite completes in under 5 seconds
    And every live or eval scenario is deselected

  @live
  Scenario: Live suite is skipped unless explicitly enabled
    Given the environment variable LIVE_TESTS is unset
    When pytest collects live-marked scenarios
    Then all @live scenarios are skipped with a clear reason
    And the run does not hang waiting on a model
optimal_implementation:
Project layout (Python orchestrator):

  tests/
    conftest.py
    features/
      tool_routing.feature
      code_quality.feature
    step_defs/
      test_tool_routing.py
      test_code_quality.py
    cassettes/                # vcrpy recordings, tagged by model id
  pytest.ini / pyproject.toml # markers + asyncio_mode

pyproject.toml (markers + asyncio):

  [tool.pytest.ini_options]
  asyncio_mode = "auto"
  markers = [
    "mocked: deterministic, no real model",
    "live: requires real model (LIVE_TESTS=1)",
    "gpu: requires a GPU",
    "eval: execution-oracle benchmark",
  ]
  addopts = "-m 'not live and not eval' --timeout=30"

conftest.py (fixtures):

  import os, pytest, respx, httpx
  from deepeval.metrics import GEval
  from deepeval.test_case import LLMTestCase, LLMTestCaseParams

  def _live_enabled():
      return os.getenv("LIVE_TESTS") == "1"

  @pytest.fixture
  def fake_model(respx_mock):
      # Mock the OpenAI-compatible HTTP seam; return a fixed tool call.
      def _set(tool_name, arguments):
          body = {"choices": [{"message": {"tool_calls": [
              {"type": "function", "function": {"name": tool_name,
               "arguments": json.dumps(arguments)}}]}}]}
          respx_mock.post("http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions").mock(
              return_value=httpx.Response(200, json=body))
      return _set

  @pytest.fixture
  def real_model():
      if not _live_enabled():
          pytest.skip("LIVE_TESTS=1 required")
      from local_claw.models import load_gemma
      m = load_gemma()
      yield m
      m.close()  # await/teardown completes before loop closes

  def assert_geval(input_text, output_text, threshold=0.8):
      metric = GEval(
          name="Coherence",
          model="gpt-4o-mini",          # cross-family judge, NOT Gemma/Qwen
          evaluation_params=[LLMTestCaseParams.INPUT, LLMTestCaseParams.ACTUAL_OUTPUT],
          criteria="Is the summary coherent and faithful to the input code?",
          threshold=threshold)
      tc = LLMTestCase(input=input_text, actual_output=output_text)
      metric.measure(tc)
      assert metric.score >= threshold, metric.reason

features/tool_routing.feature: (Scenario Outline parametrized over tool types)

  Feature: Tool routing
    @mocked
    Scenario Outline: Route <task> to <tool>
      Given a fake LLM returns tool "<tool>" with valid args
      When the agent handles "<task>"
      Then the MCP call name is "<tool>"
      And the call args match the "<tool>" schema

      Examples:
        | task                  | tool       |
        | edit app.py           | edit_file  |
        | run the test suite    | run_tests  |
        | search for TODO       | grep_code  |

step_defs/test_tool_routing.py (property assertion + outline binding):

  from pytest_bdd import scenarios, given, when, then, parsers
  from jsonschema import validate
  from local_claw.schemas import TOOL_SCHEMAS
  scenarios("../features/tool_routing.feature")

  @given(parsers.parse('a fake LLM returns tool "{tool}" with valid args'),
         target_fixture="routed")
  def _given(tool, fake_model, agent):
      fake_model(tool, sample_args_for(tool))
      return {"tool": tool}

  @when(parsers.parse('the agent handles "{task}"'))
  def _when(task, agent, routed):
      routed["call"] = agent.handle(task)   # returns the emitted MCP tool call

  @then(parsers.parse('the MCP call name is "{tool}"'))
  def _then_name(tool, routed):
      assert routed["call"].name == tool

  @then(parsers.parse('the call args match the "{tool}" schema'))
  def _then_schema(tool, routed):
      validate(instance=routed["call"].arguments, schema=TOOL_SCHEMAS[tool])

Step-by-step logic: (1) default CI runs '-m "not live and not eval"' so only mocked tests execute, GPU-free, in seconds; (2) unit steps assert parsed structure + jsonschema, never prose; (3) integration steps gate on real_model (skip unless LIVE_TESTS=1) and use assert_geval with a cross-family judge; (4) eval steps shell out to the target language's runner and parse FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS; (5) every cassette and live test is tagged with the model id so drift is detectable; (6) async teardown closes clients/subprocesses before yielding so the event loop never closes mid-cleanup.
sota_improvements: Property-based testing with Hypothesis instead of only hand-authored scenarios: generate adversarial/edge-case prompt and tool-argument inputs (empty strings, unicode, oversized payloads, malformed paths) and assert invariants (agent never emits an out-of-schema tool call, never crashes the orchestrator) - far broader coverage than enumerated Scenario Outlines.

Execution-trace evaluation, not just final-answer scoring: evaluate whether the agent took the right intermediate steps (correct tool sequence, no redundant calls, recovered from a failed tool) using AgentBench/SWE-agent-style trajectory scoring, catching agents that reach the right answer by the wrong (unrepeatable) path.

Multi-sample pass@k CI gate with statistical significance: run n >> k samples per eval task and gate on the unbiased pass@k estimator (Chen et al. 2021: 1 - C(n-c,k)/C(n,k)) rather than a single run, eliminating single-shot flakiness; flag a regression only when the CI of pass@k drops below the baseline's CI.

Golden-dataset drift detection: keep a curated gold set and periodically (nightly/weekly) compare current model outputs against it via the LLM-judge and structural metrics; alert when aggregate scores degrade, catching silent model/cassette drift before it reaches production.

Synthetic adversarial scenario generation: use the model itself (or a stronger cross-family model) to author new Gherkin scenarios and Scenario Outline rows that probe failure modes, expanding the behavioral suite automatically while keeping a human/judge gate on the generated cases.

Cross-family LLM judge with human calibration: institutionalize the no-self-judge rule (Gemma never judges Gemma) by always selecting a different-family judge and recalibrating judge thresholds against a small human-labeled set each release, directly countering self-preference bias (arxiv:2410.21819).
